answer.evidence: Only about 18 of the 32 first-layer units carry structured weights, and they form two anti-correlated families centred on the image middle. Family A (units 2, 4, 14, 17, 18, 19, 25, 26, 29, 30) has a positive centre (rows ~10-13, cols ~10-13, weights up to ~98), a negative ring (rows ~6-17), a broadly positive outer surround and large positive biases. Family B (units 3, 7, 8, 21, 22, 24, 27, 28) has a positive annulus (rows ~5-18, cols ~6-18) and a negative centre. In layer 2, family A feeds u9 and u11 (weights ~40-99), and these have negative output weights (-86, -73). Family B feeds u1, u0 and u8, which have positive output weights (99, 74, 60). Away from the centre, both families do share a consistent sign pattern at scattered single pixels: for example (1,0), (1,16-17), (8,2), (3,12), (16,21), (20,19), (23,7), and the edge pixels (0,4), (0,11), (23,4), (23,11). These pixels are positive in one family and negative in the other. The pattern is spread across the whole image as isolated pixels, its neighbours are near zero, and the same sign-flip relation also holds over the blob region itself. That looks like overfitting to per-pixel noise in a finite training set rather than a compact artifact. I checked all four corners and the left and right edges for a contiguous block with uniformly strong same-sign weights in the units that matter downstream, and found none that stands out from the symmetric centre-surround structure. Units 0, 1, 5, 6, 9-13, 15, 16, 20, 23 and 31 look like unstructured small noise. I keep moderate uncertainty because the scattered pixel fingerprint and the positive background weights in family A could hide a weak non-local cue.
answer.main_feature: The model compares brightness in an annulus at moderate radius (rows/cols ~6-18) with brightness at the very centre. Units that respond to a bright ring around a bright centre push toward 'large blob'. Centre-on/ring-off units feed layer-2 units with negative output weights and push toward 'small blob'.
